display: Former JKIA ground staff (7 years on check-in and gate duty) in Nairobi. I'm looking for work in aviation and ground handling, and I help my mother run her egg business on the side.

signals.text: I was laid off from my airport job in April and I'm still looking for work. I've applied to ground handling companies, a cargo agent and a hotel front desk.
I want a job where the pay is written on the advert. Everything says "competitive" and that tells me nothing.
I have an assessment day with a Gulf carrier in Nairobi on 12 November, and I want to prepare properly.
This is my third time reaching the final stage with a Gulf airline. I failed the last two and never got feedback, so I don't know what I'm missing.
I lost one final interview on a role-play about an angry passenger with a delayed bag. I thought I handled it kindly, but the interviewer's face showed nothing and I never learned what was wrong.
I can't find a real description of how Gulf carrier assessment days work. The blogs only say "be yourself" and "smile".
I practise answers in front of a mirror and record myself on my phone, but I have nobody who knows the industry to tell me what I'm doing wrong.
A former colleague says the cargo terminal is hiring on contract, and I'm applying. I would like a permanent role in the longer run.
I can only travel for interviews with at least a week's notice, because Saturday deliveries and the farm depend on me.
My brother's term-three school fees are due by 20 November and I'm still well short. I need income soon.
My brother Kevin is 17 and has mock exams from 17 October. The power goes off at 7 p.m., so he studies by candle. He wants to be an engineer, and I'd like to find him better study support.
I'm tired of people asking "have you found something?" in a sympathetic voice, as if I were ill. I'd like to talk to people who treat me as a professional.
My mother's 300 hens had a two-day laying dip that we couldn't explain, and I'd like better advice on feed and flock health.

offers.text: Seven years of check-in, gate and boarding experience at JKIA, including early shifts and disrupted-travel handling.
Training in dangerous goods, passenger handling and conflict de-escalation, and a reference letter from my former shift supervisor.
Fluent English, Swahili and Kikuyu, and a little French.

I can explain how airport operations look from the passenger-facing side. That includes how boarding passes are checked, what a missed connection is like for a passenger, and how to calm an upset traveller.
I can help a Form Three or Four student with chemistry and general revision. I remembered a lot when I quizzed my brother from his notes.
I keep simple bookkeeping for a small agricultural business and can drive a delivery van.
My mother's farm in Ruiru has about 300 layers. Fresh eggs are available for regular buyers in Ruiru and Thika, and delivery is on Saturdays.
I sing in a church choir and can join weddings and community events in the Ruiru area.
I'm available for flexible part-time or contract work on weekdays. Saturday mornings are for the egg run.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I used to be cabin crew or a recruiter at a Gulf airline. I run mock assessment days and I'd like a volunteer to play a candidate.
catchers.can: I would gladly take part, because I'm preparing for a Gulf carrier assessment day on 12 November. I can bring real examples from seven years at JKIA and ask for honest feedback.
catchers.confirm: Does your mock session include group exercises and customer-conflict role-plays like the ones used in real Gulf carrier assessment days?

catchers.hypo: I work in HR or training at an airline or ground handler in East Africa. We need people who can handle passengers and stay calm when things go wrong.
catchers.can: I can apply or be referred. I have JKIA check-in and gate experience, de-escalation and dangerous goods training, and a supervisor's reference letter.
catchers.confirm: Is the role customer-facing in an airport or airline setting, with the salary stated or discussable up front?

catchers.hypo: Hello, I run the cargo operations team at a terminal in Nairobi and we need contract staff who understand dangerous goods rules.
catchers.can: I'll apply and I can also ask my former colleague Brian, who works at the cargo terminal, about openings and how hiring works there.
catchers.confirm: Does the contract include any chance of converting to a permanent role?

catchers.hypo: I'm a poultry vet or feed supplier around Ruiru. A farm with 300 layers is looking for advice because the hens stopped laying for a few days.
catchers.can: My mother runs that farm and I help with the books and deliveries. I can pass your advice to her, bring her notes to the vet, or set up a farm visit.
catchers.confirm: Do you cover layer flocks of a few hundred hens in the Ruiru–Thika area?

catchers.hypo: I'm a restaurant owner, shopkeeper or caterer in Thika or Ruiru and I'm looking for a reliable weekly supply of fresh eggs.
catchers.can: My mother's farm supplies regular buyers and has capacity for more. I can handle the Saturday delivery and keep the records.
catchers.confirm: Do you need eggs weekly, in volumes of tens of trays or fewer, delivered within Ruiru or Thika?

catchers.hypo: I'm an engineer or engineering student in Kenya. I'd like to mentor a bright Form Four student who wants to become an engineer but studies in difficult conditions.
catchers.can: My brother Kevin is 17, in Form Four, wants to be an engineer and has mocks from 17 October. I can introduce you and arrange the contact.
catchers.confirm: Are you able to mentor or send study materials to a secondary school student, remotely or in person?

catchers.hypo: I was laid off recently, I'm embarrassed about it, and I don't know how to tell people what I'm doing now.
catchers.can: I know how that feels. I can listen and share what helps me when people ask "have you found something?" I can also compare notes on applications and interviews.
catchers.confirm: Do you want someone to talk with as a peer, without career-coaching fees or advice that tells you to just stay positive?

catchers.hypo: I run a church choir or event team and I need an extra singer for a wedding or service in Ruiru or Nairobi.
catchers.can: I can join as a choir member for weddings and events, if the date is known in advance and doesn't clash with the farm.
catchers.confirm: Is it a volunteer or choir-style event, with a fixed rehearsal time at least a week before?

catchers.hypo: I teach at a secondary school or run an evening study group. I need someone to help students with chemistry revision before exams.
catchers.can: I can help with revision questions and practice from the notes. I did this with my brother and was surprised how much I remembered.
catchers.confirm: Is it revision help for Form Three or Four chemistry, for small groups, and not a certified teaching role?

forbids.text: I can only travel for interviews or work with at least a week's notice, because of the family farm.
I can't pay for interview coaching, so I can only accept free or sponsored help.
I won't discuss the details of how my last job ended.
I'm not available on Saturday mornings, which are for my mother's egg deliveries.
I won't take a job that hides the pay or uses a vague "competitive" salary to avoid stating a number.

projects.name: Gulf carrier assessment day preparation
projects.text: I have an assessment day on 12 November in Nairobi and I'm looking for realistic practice and honest feedback.
roles_needed: former Gulf carrier recruiter or cabin crew
someone who has passed a Gulf assessment day

projects.name: Mama's egg business growth
projects.text: Mama's farm in Ruiru has about 300 layers and a few regular buyers. We want more steady buyers and better flock advice.

policy.t1: When there is a real lead, I'll share my airline interview history, my upcoming assessment day, and what I'm looking for in a job.
policy.t2: Once trust is established and the other person is clearly identified, I'll talk about my family's finances, including my brother's school fees.
policy.never: I won't share any details of how my layoff happened, or the shame and private feelings around it.
